questions.question: 17 is related to 21 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 22 is related to 36. To which of the following is 29 related, following the same logic? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.questionHtml: 17 is related to 21 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 22 is related to 36. To which of the following is 29 related, following the same logic? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.solution: Logic: (1st number - 10) × 3 = 2nd number. Similarly, for 29 ∶ ? ⇒ (29 - 10) × 3 = 19 × 3 = 57.

questions.question: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusion(s) logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some eagles are sparrows. All sparrows are parrots. No parrot is a penguin. Conclusions: (I) Some parrots are eagles. (II) No penguin is a sparrow.
questions.questionHtml:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if
it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusion(s) logically follow(s) from the
statements.
Statements:
Some eagles are sparrows.
All sparrows are parrots.
No parrot is a penguin.
Conclusions:
(I) Some parrots are eagles.
(II) No penguin is a sparrow.

options.text: Both conclusions I and II follow.
options.html: Both conclusions I and II follow.

options.text: Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
options.html: Neither conclusion I nor II follows.

questions.solution:
Conclusions:

I. Some parrots are eagles → Follow (As some eagles are sparrows and all sparrows are parrots. As some part of eagles is common with sparrows which whole comes in parrots, therefore it is true.)

II. No penguin is a sparrow → Follow (As all sparrows are parrots and no parrot is a penguin. As whole sparrows comes in parrots which cannot be penguin, therefore it is true.)

∴ Here, Both conclusions I and II follow.

questions.question: How many triangles are there in the given figure?
questions.questionHtml: How many triangles are there in the given figure?
questions.solution:
1) Total triangles = [Number of parts × (1 + Number of parts)] ÷ 2

= [2 × (1 + 2)] ÷ 2

= [2 × 3] ÷ 2

= 6 ÷ 2

= 3

As there are 4 same types of triangles, therefore total number of triangles will be (3 × 4) = 12 

2) As marked there are total 3 triangles.

Thus, there are total (12 + 3) = 15 triangles.

questions.question: Two sets of numbers are given below. In each set of numbers, certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number result(s) in the second number. Similarly, certain mathematical operation(s) on the second number result(s) in the third number and so on. Which of the given options follows the same set of operations as in the given sets? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) 11 – 14 – 8 – 17; 12 – 15 – 9 – 18
questions.questionHtml:
Two sets of numbers are given below. In each set of numbers, certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number
result(s) in the second number. Similarly, certain mathematical operation(s) on the second number result(s) in the third
number and so on. Which of the given options follows the same set of operations as in the given sets?
(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent
digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1
and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
11 – 14 – 8 – 17; 12 – 15 – 9 – 18
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

11 – 14 – 8 – 17

11 + 3 = 14

14 - 6 = 8

8 + 9 = 17

Option 4) 6 – 9 – 3 – 12

6 + 3 = 9

9 - 6 = 3

3 + 9 = 12

Thus, out of all the options '6 – 9 – 3 – 12' follows the same logic as given.

questions.question: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if '+' and '−' are interchanged and '×' and '÷' are interchanged? 1205 × 5 + 35 − 197 ÷ 18 = ?
questions.questionHtml:
What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if '+' and '−' are interchanged and '×' and '÷' are interchanged?

1205 × 5 + 35 − 197 ÷  18 = ?
questions.solution:
Given equation: 1205 × 5 + 35 − 197 ÷ 18 = ?

After interchanging the signs then:

⇒ 1205 ÷ 5 - 35 + 197 × 18 = ?

⇒ ? = 241 - 35 + 197 × 18 ⇒ ? = 241 - 35 + 3546 ⇒ ? = 3787 - 35 = 3752

questions.question: In a certain code language, ‘A + B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’; ‘A − B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’; ‘A × B’ means ‘A is the wife of B’ and ‘A ÷ B’ means ‘A is the father of B’. Based on the above, how is A related to D if ‘A × B ÷ C × D’?
questions.questionHtml:
In a certain code language,
‘A + B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’;
‘A − B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’;
‘A × B’ means ‘A is the wife of B’ and
‘A ÷ B’ means ‘A is the father of B’.
Based on the above, how is A related to D if ‘A × B ÷ C × D’?
questions.solution: Thus, A is D's wife’s mother or mother-in-law.

The logic followed here is: (Second Number × 6) + 1 = First Number
